## What Problem This Solves

Placement moves, prepared-environment binding, retirement, and standing-grant preparation still perform SQLite work on the Gateway thread. Awaited persistence must preserve live authority, accepted-write ordering, and successful session deletion when orphan cleanup retires the same placement first.

## User Impact

Placement and approval preparation use the existing database workers while retaining revocation and cancellation behavior. No schema, persisted-format, retention, durability, configuration, or environment-variable changes are introduced. Released synchronous SDK signatures remain available; worker failures do not fall back to native persistence. Remaining ordinary getter and policy-preparation callers stay in stacked PR #166445.

## Why This Change Was Made

The placement actor owns move/bind/retirement writes, and the approval reader prepares joined grant facts. Transactions remain synchronous. Physical ownership and live authorization are checked after waits and immediately before commit; accepted writes retain FIFO settlement through shutdown. Placement mutations with unknown outcomes are never replayed. New abandonment intents check the live runner against transaction-local source facts, while callers joining an existing durable intent retain its original decision.

The landing repairs preserve refreshed profile authority, invalidate the embedded fallback placement cache when its database owner retires, and keep conditional Move cancellation from replacing the original Stop error. Retirement recognizes an already-absent row inside the worker transaction without publishing a fabricated transition. Present rows still require the exact state, generation, and null claim fields; the released synchronous method remains strict. Successful retirement adds no SQL. The recovery test now uses its existing asynchronous session/Gateway-home cleanup owner instead of closing SQLite prematurely in a competing hook.

Released Gateway/SDK surfaces were checked against `v2026.10.1-beta.1` and `v2026.9.8`. Optional async companions, compatibility records, and type assertions preserve callers until the next SDK major. Standing-grant `consume` remains the permanent synchronous final transport guard, not a deprecated preparation API.
